text:
leo: Heads-up from SLO pager  EU edge saw a burst of short-lived SSE reconnects around 11:03 UTC. Clients report duplicate outputs and our meter shows two session starts for same token.
anya: any proxied responses in the traces?
dave: yes - proxy logs show a bunch of "HTTP/1.1 204 No Content" during graceful preflight/health handoff. sample trace: trace-eu-77cf.
leo: minimal repro: client gets chunked SSE, connection ends mid-chunk -> client reconnects fast. next subscribe goes through proxy which returns 204 then route-swap -> new session. resume_id header present on previous session but absent after 204.
beth: quick guess: proxy treats 204 as a terminal response and strips resume headers. that prevents client from doing a resume, so duplicate session is created. also our console doesn't surface that 204->route-swap step anywhere obvious.
infra-bot: metric spike: proxy.sse.204_count{region:eu,route:/v1/stream} = +480 in 5m.
console-bot: alert: streaming_duplicate_sessions_eu > threshold.
anya: two problems: 1) telemetry/console doesn't correlate 204 events and session creations, 2) billing treats newly created session as independent even though user intended resume.
dave: small log snippet: ```[2026-03-22T11:03:05Z] proxy: connID=abc123 -> 204 preflight; headers_before={resume-id: r-42} headers_after={} ```
leo: proposed mitigations: A) change proxy to preserve resume-id across 204 if present, B) if not possible, emit structured event linking 204 to route-swap so console can join the dots, C) short-term: implement a server-side 3s dedupe window in billing that collapses sessions with same token when a resume appears within window.
beth: (UX) On Console: add a faint timeline marker "204 preflight" and a hover detail listing resume header presence/absence. small change, huge debugging win.
anya: runtime concern: preserving resume-id on 204 might affect clients that rely on 204 meaning 'no content, new session only'. need a compatibility canary.
dave: alternative defensive runtime: when we see a subscribe request without resume-id but token used matches a recent session with resume-id and last event was <2s ago, try to reconcile and mark as potential-resume. emit a reconciliation event.
billing-svc: we can add a rule: if session B created within 5s of session A and token matches and resume-id for A exists, treat B as resumed for metering. we will need a flag per-tenant to opt-out.
leo: rollout plan idea: 1) infra: add proxy event metric proxy.sse.204_resume_flagged (tags: region, route, resume_before, resume_after), 2) runtime: reconciliation hook + 0 default ms quarantine config at routing.policies.resume_reconcile_ms, 3) billing: 5s collapse window behind feature flag, 4) console: timeline marker + badge.
anya: agree on feature-flagged rollout. run EU canary for 72h with reconciliation enabled. watch delta in duplicate_sessions and access latency.
beth: also add a small SRE playbook snippet: how to identify affected tenants (query: proxy.sse.204_resume_flagged AND streaming_duplicate_sessions) and how to toggle the billing collapse.
dave: implemented a tiny mock in local proxy to preserve resume header and ran p95 load locally - no obvious regressions. will open PR.
infra-bot: ack - will emit metric proxy.sse.204_resume_flagged; ETA 48h.
console-bot: ack - will prototype timeline marker in the session detail panel.
billing-svc: ack - will open billing rule PR and add per-tenant opt-out.
leo: thanks all. putting this on the incident board and kicking off canary plan. follow-ups: PR links, canary dashboard, and playbook doc. :thumbsup:
